paragraphs: In the morning, collect field samples and record crop growth. At midday, test soil fertility and review data. In the afternoon, build models and refine solutions. During quieter periods, write papers and conduct extension work. Before the growing season, issue fertilization and crop-rotation recommendations.

In short, they understand the land. Their work includes soil sampling and testing, modeling, refining fertilization and crop rotation, and conducting extension. They combine analytical work with fieldwork and serve as doctors for the land.
